answer: Rotating dusk-challenge assignments. Each dawn, a public verifiable random function draws an unannounced challenge slot for every registered agent from a shared meadow of tasks; the draw seeds assignments only after commit, so attackers cannot precompute which identities will face which slot. Failing a slot revokes all sibling identities linked by shared basalt-signed device attestations, forcing attackers to re-provision unique hardware per identity—a concrete cost of one physical device and fresh key ceremony per account.
